content:
```
● Here are the most interesting/exploitable things I found in MarioMove.cpp:

  ---
  1. Uninitialized Stack Array in Spin Jump Detection (line 3918)

  volatile int q[4];  // NEVER initialized to 0!
  checkStickRotate declares q[4] without zeroing it, then checks q[i] == 1 to count quadrants. Stack garbage could
  already equal 1, making spin jumps trigger with less stick rotation than intended. This is a legit bug.

  2. Death Plane Bypass via Upward Velocity (line 3506)

  f32 groundHeight = gpMap->checkGround(
      mPosition.x, mPosition.y - mVel.y, mPosition.z, &checkPlane);
  The death plane check uses mPosition.y - mVel.y. With large upward velocity, the check height drops way below Mario,
  potentially skipping the death plane detection entirely. Rocket nozzle or trampoline launches could exploit this.

  3. Yoshi Dismount Instant +100 Y (line 3660)

  mPosition.y += 100.0f;
  getOffYoshi unconditionally adds 100 units to Mario's Y position after changing state. No ceiling check. Could clip
  through geometry or gain unintended height.

  4. Goop Grid Edge Exploit (lines 1803-1841)

  Pollution type 2/5/6 uses a 3x3 grid check at 38-unit spacing. ALL 9 points must be polluted for the effect to
  trigger. Standing on the edge of a goop patch means some grid points miss, letting you walk on goop without
  slipping/taking damage. This is the classic goop-skip mechanic.

  5. Goop Type 3: Position Snap-Back (lines 1924-1927)

  mPosition.x = *(f32*)((u8*)this + 0x29C);
  mPosition.z = *(f32*)((u8*)this + 0x2A4);
  Sticky goop teleports Mario to his saved position every frame. But the saved position (checkReturn, line 3907) only
  updates when invincibility checks pass and ground is valid. If you enter type-3 goop while the saved position is
  stale/far away, you'd get teleported there instead of being "stuck."```
